reason: The after-meal pancreatic cells contain insulin and sit beside blood, so using the blood there should start the muscle-storage route.
expectation: Insulin will be released into the blood.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals route is also a goal, but I will start with the after-meal condition.

effect: Insulin is now in the blood and its route points toward muscle, so I can follow the after-meal goal.
reaction: The route to muscle makes the next step clear.
reason: The muscle fibres have receptors for blood-carried insulin and glucose nearby.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin will help the muscle take in and store glucose.

effect: The muscle has stored glucose, completing the after-meal goal; I can now follow the between-meals route.
reaction: It was useful to see that insulin stays outside the cells rather than becoming part of the store.
reason: The between-meals pancreatic cells contain glucagon and can release it into the blood.
expectation: Glucagon will be released into the blood as a message to the liver.

effect: Glucagon is in the blood and is shown travelling toward the liver, so I can use it with the liver's carbohydrate store.
reaction: The labelled message makes its purpose clear.
reason: The story says glucagon tells the liver to release stored glucose between meals.
expectation: The liver will break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose into the blood, completing the between-meals goal and showing how its store can supply fuel.
reaction: The shrinking store made the result easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using glucagon with the liver store was most worthwhile because it showed how stored glucose reaches the blood between meals.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing each message into blood felt a little repetitive, although the two conditions and messages were different.

surprise.text: I found it useful that insulin stayed outside the muscle cells: it was a message, not material for the carbohydrate store.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the labels and pictures explained why each pairing was needed.

continue.text: I would continue to see how other organs respond to chemical messages. Comparing the two conditions made this chapter understandable, though the pairings were fairly predictable.
